questions.question: Explain two ways in which education helps to reduce inequality.
questions.expected_answer: Any two: increases skills and productivity, leading to employment and higher income; gives access to skilled jobs that pay more; breaks the cycle of poverty across generations; helps people start businesses; improves health, financial decisions and knowledge of rights.

questions.question: Name three government programmes that widen access to education and say what each does.
questions.expected_answer: Any three: no-fee schools (no school fees in the poorest communities); National School Nutrition Programme (daily cooked meal); scholar transport (transport for rural learners); free textbooks/DBE workbooks; NSFAS (bursaries for poor students at universities and TVET colleges); Funza Lushaka (bursaries for student teachers); Grade R/ECD.

questions.question: What is the difference between a TVET college course and a learnership, and why are artisans important to the economy?
questions.expected_answer: A TVET college offers practical vocational courses mainly in a college setting; a learnership combines classroom learning with paid practical work in a workplace. Artisans such as electricians, plumbers and mechanics are in short supply, are needed for infrastructure and industry, can earn good incomes and can start businesses that create jobs.
